public_rationale: Reporting corroborates roughly $34 billion in expenses and identifies $20.92 billion as operating loss. It identifies roughly $13 billion as revenue, while net loss was much larger. These are material problems with the sentence, but they do not establish the actual EBITDA margin. Without a reconciliation, neither confirming nor rejecting negative 160% as EBITDA is justified.
limitations: Audited status is reported by the sources; the underlying audit was not inspected.
Secondary reports partly share the same leaked-document origin and are not wholly independent confirmations.
The expense component is corroborated; the central EBITDA component remains unsettled.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI's audited 2025 financials show $34 billion in expenses and an EBITDA margin of negative 160%.

statement.excerpt: Let me give you a very straightforward example from my own story on OpenAI’s audited 2025 financials, when it had $34 billion of expenses and $13.07 billion in losses, for an EBITDA of $20.92 billion, or an EBITDA margin of negative 160%.

our_interpretation: Assess the 2025 annual results, not annualized revenue or a later forecast.
The negative margin and surrounding discussion imply negative EBITDA, despite the missing minus sign before $20.92 billion.
Preserve the explicit reference to $13.07 billion in losses as a possible labeling error; do not silently change it to revenue.
An audited financial statement does not necessarily report EBITDA. A reconciliation is needed before treating operating loss as EBITDA.
criteria.support_condition: The annual statements establish approximately $34 billion in expenses, and a valid EBITDA reconciliation establishes approximately negative $20.92 billion and a margin rounding to negative 160%. The stated loss figure must also be reconciled.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable annual statements and an EBITDA reconciliation establish materially different expenses or an EBITDA margin that does not round to negative 160%. A mislabeled input alone does not establish that the margin is false.

evidence.explanation: The reported net loss also differs from $13.07 billion. Net loss is a different metric and cannot decide the EBITDA-margin claim.
